title: Nickel Asia subsidiaries bag seven awards at inaugural TSM Excellence AwardsNickel Asia subsidiaries bag seven awards at inaugural TSM Excellence Awards - The Manila Times
content: NICKEL Asia Corp. (NAC), through subsidiaries Rio Tuba Nickel Mining Corp. (RTNMC) and Taganito Mining Corp. (TMC), received seven awards at the Philippines’ inaugural Towards Sustainable Mining (TSM) Excellence Awards on Oct. 27 at Conrad Manila. The ceremony was part of the Mining Philippines International Conference and Exhibition organized by the Chamber of Mines of the Philippines (COMP). COMP Chairman Michael Toledo said the awards recognize companies demonstrating responsible mining through their decisions, systems, and standards. The TSM framework recognizes mining companies through independently verified assessments. Scores of 4.5 to 5.0 qualify for gold, while 3.5 to 4.49 earn silver. RTNMC received four gold awards, including Excellence in Community Partnership and Shared Development, Safety Leadership and Zero Harm, and Water Stewardship and Watershed Responsibility. It was also the sole gold recipient in the Cross-Cutting category, the evening’s top award. TMC earned gold in Excellence in Community Partnership and Shared Development, and silver awards in Safety Leadership and Zero Harm and the Cross-Cutting category. NAC Senior Vice President for Sustainability, Risk Management and Corporate Affairs Jose Bayani Baylon said the recognition demonstrates Filipinos’ ability to meet international mining standards, emphasizing the importance of communicating the industry’s responsible practices. The Philippines adopted TSM through COMP in 2017, becoming the first Asian country to implement the internationally recognized sustainability framework.

Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE:TSM | TSM Price Prediction) rose 6.26% in U.S. trading on November 6, 2026. The move came one day after a 10.78% drop to $353.10. The catalyst was a report that TSMC recently began drawing up plans to make vertically stacked DRAM at the request of its top customer, NVIDIA (NASDAQ:NVDA). The report cited two people with direct knowledge of the matter. Neither company has confirmed it, and TSMC does not comment on market speculation. The rest of the chip group also rebounded. The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ:SMH) rose 3.52%, NVIDIA gained 2.78% to $186.64, and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) added 5.12%. TSMC’s ADR rose more than the sector, topping out at a 7.7% gain early in the session, but it still finished the week down 7.61%. Taiwan’s market had already closed when the report came out. Nothing has been signed or announced. TSMC is reportedly deciding whether to build new fabs or buy and retool an existing site, similar to Micron’s $1.8 billion purchase of a Powerchip fab in Taiwan in March. The effort is reportedly led by Hsu Kuo-chin, a TSMC vice president who runs advanced packaging and previously ran Micron’s regional operations. Vertically stacked DRAM puts memory cells on top of one another within a single chip. High-bandwidth memory (HBM) is a different product that stacks whole memory chips. TSMC has not said how much it might invest or when production could begin. Its 2026 capital budget is already $60 billion to $64 billion, and a memory fab would add to that. Management did not discuss making memory on its October 15 earnings call. NVIDIA has a clear reason to want another source. Its supply obligations reached $279.0 billion, mostly for the memory that goes into Vera Rubin, and its CFO said: “The magnitude of the price increase has exceeded our prior expectations.” A second supplier would give NVIDIA more leverage over memory makers, although no new supply would arrive in time to affect results for years. Micron’s gain on Friday shows no sign that the report hurt memory stocks. Its 22.01% weekly loss came from the earlier selloff. Micron also forecasts $61.5 billion in quarterly revenue and is already co-designing HBM4E with NVIDIA. TSMC holds patents on vertical DRAM. The real difficulty is moving from patents to mass production with almost no defects. Samsung, SK hynix and Micron dominate memory, and the business swings between booms and busts. Memory has also historically made thinner margins than leading-edge logic, while TSMC posted a 66.4% gross margin last quarter. Building new capacity takes a long time. Micron expects first wafers from its new Idaho fab in mid-calendar 2027 and says meaningful supply growth will take a few more quarters after that. The logic business remains the core of the investment case. TSMC forecasts fourth-quarter revenue of $52.3 billion to $54.3 billion, up from $46.72 billion, and expects full-year 2026 growth of about 44%. The memory report is a long-term possibility that isn’t priced into those numbers. Even after Friday’s rebound, the ADR is down 20.54% over one month, so the selloff did more to lower the price than the report did to lift it. Taiwan Semiconductor, the world's largest chip foundry, is considering expanding its business into advanced storage chip manufacturing and has, at the request of its largest customer NVIDIA, begun formulating plans to produce 3D DRAM (three-dimensional dynamic random-access memory). The Zhitong Finance APP has learned that, according to media reports, Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US), the world's largest chip foundry, is considering expanding its business into advanced storage chip manufacturing and has, at the request of its largest customer NVIDIA (NVDA.US), begun formulating plans to produce 3D DRAM (three-dimensional dynamic random-access memory). If this plan is ultimately implemented, Taiwan Semiconductor could further expand its influence in the artificial intelligence (AI) hardware supply chain. According to media reports citing two insiders, Taiwan Semiconductor has recently begun studying production plans for 3D DRAM. This move stems from NVIDIA's demand for advanced memory chips and reflects that AI chip designers are actively seeking to diversify their sources of critical components. 3D DRAM is an advanced memory chip technology that employs a three-dimensional architecture, aiming to increase storage density through novel cell layouts and manufacturing processes, while providing more technological options for future high-performance computing systems. For Taiwan Semiconductor, which has long focused on logic chip foundry and advanced packaging, entering advanced DRAM manufacturing would mean further expanding its business portfolio. Currently, Taiwan Semiconductor dominates the global advanced logic chip manufacturing sector and is also a key manufacturing partner for NVIDIA's AI accelerators. If it further enters the advanced memory chip production field in the future, Taiwan Semiconductor will have the opportunity to play a role in more critical segments of AI computing hardware. This potential business expansion comes at a time when the global memory chip market is facing severe supply constraints. As the boom in generative AI and data center construction continues, demand for high-performance computing hardware and associated memory chips is surging, tightening supply and driving prices sharply higher. For AI chip designers such as NVIDIA, memory chips are a critical component that determines the performance and production scale of computing systems. Supply shortages could not only drive up hardware manufacturing costs but also constrain the pace of AI infrastructure deployment. Consequently, major tech companies, including NVIDIA and Apple (AAPL.US), are actively seeking additional sources of memory chip supply to mitigate supply chain risks. The impact of rising storage chip prices has also begun to ripple through the consumer electronics market. Earlier this year, Apple raised the prices of some products, citing higher storage costs, highlighting that the tight supply of storage chips is no longer confined to the AI server sector but is affecting a broader range of electronic product markets. Against this backdrop, NVIDIA is urging Taiwan Semiconductor to research 3D DRAM production, which may help it establish a more diversified advanced storage chip supply system in the future. However, the relevant plans are currently still in the preliminary research and planning stages. The report did not disclose the scale of funding Taiwan Semiconductor plans to invest, its potential production capacity, the mass-production timeline, or whether it will formally launch commercial production in the future. Furthermore, 3D DRAM is not entirely the same technological route as High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which is widely used in current AI accelerators, and Taiwan Semiconductor's research into 3D DRAM production does not mean it has decided to enter the existing HBM market. title: TSMC Stock (TSM) Falls 10.8% as Chip Stocks Slide (Nov 5) - Gotrade
content: Gotrade News - In the latest TSMC stock news, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) fell 10.78% to close at $353.10 on Thursday, November 5, 2026, as a sell-off in chip stocks ran into a second day. TSMC itself had no news, according to TIKR, which tied the drop in TSMC stock to fears of a slower AI build-out after Democrats' larger-than-expected midterm wins. Regular-session close on Thursday, November 5, 2026, 4:00 p.m. New York time. Stock prices: Yahoo Finance, cross-checked against the closing price on Nasdaq.com. Volume and 30-day average volume: Nasdaq.com. 52-week range: Yahoo Finance daily highs and lows since November 6, 2025. Indices and the 10-year Treasury yield: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the same date. Follow TSM's latest price on our TSMC (TSM) stock price today page. TSM opened below Wednesday's close and sold off through the session, finishing just $1.91 above its intraday low. Trading was heavy, with volume running 282.80% above the stock's average. The drop was steeper than the broader market's. On the same November 5 session, the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% to 24,315.00, the S&P 500 lost 4.36% to 7,353.73 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 3.44% to 51,523.06, leaving TSM 5.26 percentage points behind the Nasdaq. The US 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.7 basis points to 4.84%. Chip peers fell hard as well. Nvidia (NVDA) lost 9.26%, while AMD (AMD) dropped 17.26% and Micron (MU) fell 17.46%. After the decline, TSM sits 27.56% below its 52-week high and 32.34% above its 52-week low. The drop did not come from company news: TIKR reported that TSMC had no news of its own on Thursday. Financial media tied the fall instead to a chip rout that deepened after Democrats' larger-than-expected midterm wins raised fears of a slower AI build-out. Two industry reports added pressure, as reported by TIKR. Qualcomm, a TSMC customer, warned on memory costs after Wednesday's close, and Bloomberg reported on Thursday morning that Micron had paused a $4.5 billion Taiwan plant. The selling also reflects wider doubts about AI budgets. According to The Motley Fool, recent selling pressure has raised questions about the sustainability of massive AI infrastructure spending. The next read on demand is TSMC's October revenue, which TIKR says is due next week and will be the first check on the fourth-quarter guidance. title: West Edmeston Tree No More: Its Journey To NYC Is Underway - CNY News
content: Like many, I have driven past this tree off State Route 8 in West Edmeston for years, it's almost like a local landmark or one of those "oh I know where I am" markers. Now all that's left of the 76-foot Norway Spruce are the memories and lots of pictures. This process didn't happen overnight, it's a month's long endeavor with various local state and Rockefeller Center groups coming together to bring a showstopping spectacle to New York City for millions to see. READ MORE: The 2026 Rockefeller Tree Has Been Chosen, From Central New York Shortly before 7am November 5th, cranes were in place ready to lift this year's Rockefeller Tree from the ground and onto a flatbed. Family and friends gathered at the sight surrounded by plenty of media buzz as well. Current owners of the property at 6526 New York 8 we're excited to see the joy that one tree can bring to millions of people around the world. Rebecca Decker told us once she found out the tree's history and the fact this Christmas 2026 marked the 10th anniversary of the death of the person who planted it, she didn't think twice about donating it. Decker remembered the moment someone from the Rockefeller Center first came to her door and asked about the tree. Erik Pauzé, head gardener and head tree scout for Rockefeller Center was that person. Pauzé remembered when he first saw the tree and made sure to write the address down for a potential future tree. As the hour passed by, crews began their finishing touches before the chainsaw came out. There was some laughter and at one point some were spectacle that the tree was going to come down. The chainsaw operator had a difficult time getting the saw to start. But eventually the engine came to life and the cutting started. Within five minutes, the tree was hoisted above its stump. Cheers from the crowd could be heard and I'm sure some happy tears as well. Crews took a once vertical standing tree and carefully laid it horizontal onto the flatbed. From cut to truck, the process took well over an hour. The only thing left was a plot of dirt once shadowed by the Norway Spruce. READ MORE: Santa For Seniors Returns To Bring Christmas Cheer To Seniors In Central New York Department of Transportation officials and members from the Rockefeller Center say the trip won't take long but expect a lot of attention on the way to NYC. Erik Pauzé said they will drive as far as they can today before stopping at a secure location overnight. By Saturday, the once West Edmeston tree will be in New York City for the annual meet the tree day celebration. We were told that 50 thousand lights are set to light up this tree and the official tree lighting ceremony takes place December 2nd at 7pm. title: TSMC Stock (TSM) Falls 2.2% as AI Chip Stocks Slide (Nov 4) - Gotrade
content: Gotrade News - In the latest TSMC stock news, TSMC (TSM) fell 2.24% to close at $395.75 on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, a down day for TSMC stock even as the broader US market rallied. Financial media tied the weakness in AI and data center names to worries about a backlash against the data center industry after Democrats' midterm wins. Regular-session close on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 4:00 p.m. New York time. Stock prices: Yahoo Finance, cross-checked against the closing price on Nasdaq.com. Volume and 30-day average volume: Nasdaq.com. 52-week range: Yahoo Finance daily highs and lows since November 5, 2025. Indices and the 10-year Treasury yield: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the same date. Follow TSM's latest price on our TSMC (TSM) stock price today page. TSM opened at $400.64, below the previous close of $404.80, and climbed as high as $410.59 before turning lower. It slipped to a session low of $391.61 and closed just $4.14 above that low, near the bottom of the day's range. Volume reached 14.5 million shares, 30.82% above the 11.1 million share average, so the decline came on heavier trading than usual. The move ran against the market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 3.03% to 53,356.12, the S&P 500 gained 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.44% to 25,736.51, leaving TSM 3.68 percentage points behind the Nasdaq. The US 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.8 basis points to 4.89%. Several chip names fell with TSMC. Nvidia (NVDA) lost 3.17% to $200.13, ASML (ASML) dropped 3.60% to $1,496.30 and Micron (MU) fell 7.00% to $795.23. After the session, TSM sits 18.82% below its 52-week high of $487.47 and 48.32% above its 52-week low of $266.82. No source we reviewed names a TSMC-specific reason for Wednesday's decline. The stock fell with AI-linked chip stocks while the major indices rallied. The session came the day after the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats flipped control of the House and Senate, as reported by CNBC. In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race after calling for tougher restrictions on data center development. Per CNBC, names linked to the data center build-out fell on Wednesday on worries about a backlash to the industry, while Jordan Watson, a portfolio manager at Tandem Investment Advisors, said the rotation away from artificial intelligence names "could be temporary." According to CBS News, LPL Research's Jeff Buchbinder said federal policy implications may be limited in a divided government, but that data center policy decisions sit at the state and utility-commission level, potentially increasing regulatory pressure on AI infrastructure stocks including semiconductors. TSMC's financial calendar lists its October sales report for November 10 at 1:30 p.m. Taipei time, a date GuruFocus says may change.
